advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Report cascaded parent STATUS event paths from the inbound CREATE path (mirror the UPDATE path's ApplyResult 'events') or document why the create path intentionally omits them.
evidence: apply_inbound_events.py:220 `_cascade_inbound_status_parents(tracker_dir, local_id, "open", local_status)` — return value ignored on the create path
apply_inbound_events.py:408-410 update path: `written.extend(_cascade_inbound_status_parents(...))` threads paths into the result
apply_inbound.py:129 create result payload is only `{"local_id": local_id, "create_event": str(create_path)}` — no cascaded-parent events reported
apply_inbound.py:169 update result payload carries `"events": written`
advisory.finding: On the inbound CREATE path the return value of _cascade_inbound_status_parents is discarded, so cascaded parent STATUS events are written to disk but never reported in the create ApplyResult, whereas the UPDATE path threads the same paths into ApplyResult.payload['events']. The two write surfaces report cascaded parent writes asymmetrically.
scenarios: A fresh inbound ticket landing at in_progress under an open parent: the parent's STATUS event is written but is invisible to any manifest/consumer that reads the create ApplyResult

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test with a cyclic parent chain asserting the inbound cascade terminates and writes each ancestor at most once.
evidence: apply_inbound_events.py cascade loop: `seen = {local_id}` ... `if parent_id is None or parent_id in seen: break`
ABSENCE: no test in test_inbound_status_cascade.py constructs a parent<->child (or self-parent) cycle; all fixtures build strictly acyclic chains (jira-dig-1<-2, jira-dig-10<-11<-12).
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/apply_inbound_events.py:170-172: "a ``_write_event_file`` failure propagates out of the leaf exactly as the child's own STATUS write failure already does."

ABSENCE: no test monkeypatches/forces `_write_event_file` (or the underlying write) to raise on a cascaded parent and asserts the exception propagates from `_apply_inbound_update` / `_apply_inbound_create`.
advisory.finding: The cycle-guard branch introduced by the diff (`seen = {local_id}` plus `if parent_id is None or parent_id in seen: break`) is never exercised by any test. A malformed parent chain that forms a cycle is the exact failure the guard exists to stop; a regression removing the guard would loop and/or write duplicate ancestor STATUS events, and no test would catch it.
merged_from: The diff's stated failure-posture contract — a `_write_event_file` failure on a cascaded parent 'propagates out of the leaf exactly as the child's own STATUS write failure already does' — is untested. No test injects a parent write failure to confirm the exception propagates rather than being swallowed (which would silently skip the child write and leave the I4a-invalid state the change exists to prevent).
scenarios: A Jira-derived or corrupted local store where a ticket's resolved parent chain forms a cycle (A parent of B, B parent of A).
